claims.subject: i_driveSouth_00
claims.explanation: The flow starts at i_driveSouth_00, which is connected to node_00.i_driveSouth. Node_00 then outputs to w_drive00201 (north to node_01) and w_drive00210 (east to node_10). These internal wires create a cascade: node_01 outputs to w_drive01200 (south back to node_00) and w_drive01211 (east to node_11); node_10 outputs to w_drive10200 (west back to node_00) and w_drive10211 (north to node_11); node_11 outputs to w_drive11201 (west to node_01) and w_drive11210 (south to node_10). This mesh connectivity ensures the single input event can reach every node and thus every output endpoint.

claims.subject: node_00

claims.explanation: Node_00 receives the i_driveSouth_00 event and, based on internal routing logic, can forward it to its north output (w_drive00201 to node_01) and east output (w_drive00210 to node_10). It also receives feedback from node_01 (w_drive01200) and node_10 (w_drive10200), indicating it can merge or arbitrate returning event paths.

claims.subject: node_01, node_10, node_11
claims.summary: Intermediate nodes that propagate the event through the mesh.
claims.explanation: Node_01 receives the event from node_00 via w_drive00201 and can forward it to node_11 via w_drive01211 and back to node_00 via w_drive01200. Node_10 receives from node_00 via w_drive00210 and can forward to node_11 via w_drive10211 and back to node_00 via w_drive10200. Node_11 receives from node_01 and node_10 and can forward back to node_01 via w_drive11201 and to node_10 via w_drive11210. Each node also drives its local, north, south, east, and west output endpoints.
